readmeHtml:
Documentation | Changelog | Roadmap

The web has evolved. Finally, testing has too.

Fast, easy and reliable testing for anything that runs in a browser.

Join us, we're hiring.


What is Cypress?

Installing

Install Cypress for Mac, Linux, or Windows, then get started.

npm install cypress --save-dev

or

yarn add cypress --dev

or

pnpm add cypress --save-dev

Contributing

- develop branch

Please see our Contributing Guideline which explains repo organization, linting, testing, and other steps.

License

This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT license.

Badges

Configure a badge for your project's README to show your test status or test count in the Cypress Cloud.

Or let the world know your project is using Cypress with the badge below.

[![Cypress.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/tested%20with-Cypress-04C38E.svg)](https://www.cypress.io/)

aiSummary.oneLiner: Fast, easy, and reliable testing framework for anything that runs in a browser.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Cypress is a modern testing framework designed specifically for the web. It operates directly within the browser, providing fast, reliable, and easy-to-write tests for modern web applications. The tool eliminates the flaky issues often found in older testing architectures by running in the same run-loop as the application. It supports end-to-end testing as well as component testing for major frameworks like React, Vue, Angular, and Svelte.
keyFeatures: In-browser execution: runs tests directly inside the browser for reliable, flake-free execution.
Real-time reloading: automatically reloads tests whenever changes are made to the codebase.
Time travel debugging: takes snapshots as tests run, allowing developers to hover over commands and see exactly what happened.
Component testing: provides dedicated support for testing isolated components in modern frontend frameworks.
Network traffic control: allows mocking, stubbing, and controlling edge cases without altering server code.
Dashboard integration: integrates with Cypress Cloud to record test runs, track failures, and optimize test suites.

useCases.title: End-to-end web testing
useCases.description: QA engineers can write automated tests that simulate real user interactions across an entire web application.

useCases.title: Frontend component isolation
useCases.description: React and Vue developers can test individual components in isolation without needing to load the entire application.

useCases.title: CI/CD test automation
useCases.description: DevOps teams can integrate the framework into their continuous integration pipelines to catch regressions before deployment.

useCases.title: Network failure simulation
useCases.description: Developers can easily mock server responses and simulate network delays to test how the UI handles edge cases.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers, QA engineers, and DevOps teams building and maintaining modern web applications. It is designed to be accessible to anyone writing JavaScript or TypeScript.
